glossary.definition: Whether a measure supports the intended interpretation.
The precise outcome a comparison aims to estimate.
Evidence kept out of adaptive fitting and selection for assessment of performance on unseen cases.
For probability forecasts, how closely predicted confidence matches observed outcome frequencies, distinct from judge–human label agreement.
How far evidence supports conclusions beyond studied tasks and conditions.
A retained, replayable case with expected behavior used to check for regressions on that case.
Increasing a proxy reward without achieving its intended objective.
Ordered actions, tool calls and state changes in one run.

For a specified task, population and positive class, precision is true positives divided by all predicted positives; recall is true positives divided by all actual positives. Interpret each with its denominator and error costs.
A mechanism checking a stated property; validity and coverage require separate evaluation.

reading_paths.description: Frame the decision and success criteria, identify what the evidence can establish, choose representative cases and measures, verify outcomes, compare results, then assess value and risk. This is the shared core; use the agent, data, judge or verification task paths for specialist methods.
reading_paths.title: Start here: decide what evidence you need

reading_paths.description: Use when a team has a problem but no defensible evaluation: frame the decision, bound conclusions, inspect failure evidence, then grow coverage. For an agent comparison continue with comparing-agents-without-confounding-the-result; use the section index for other foundations.
reading_paths.title: Frame an evaluation and learn from failures

reading_paths.description: Use for a reproducible agent comparison: select the benchmark, design its population and tasks, specify success and resource measures, control model–harness differences, inspect outcomes and protect integrity. For statistical estimands and confidence, also read compare-systems-confidence-and-behavior-without-mixing-estimands; it is distinct from attribution in comparing-agents-without-confounding-the-result.
reading_paths.title: Design and compare agent evaluations

reading_paths.description: Use when building an offline set: first select the population and slices, specify valid tasks, collect production-grounded cases and human judgments, then protect holdouts. Optional: generate-synthetic-cases-without-mistaking-them-for-reality for coverage gaps; generated cases are not a substitute for reality.
reading_paths.title: Build an evaluation set for a decision

reading_paths.description: Use when designing a judge: define the target and rubric, consider proxy limits, provide evidence, select a method, collect human references, validate against held-out labels, then operate and improve. Revisit agreement-truth-and-the-limits-of-evaluator-proxies when interpreting validation: agreement is not truth. Optional compare-systems-confidence-and-behavior-without-mixing-estimands clarifies comparative and calibration questions rather than judge implementation.
reading_paths.title: Build and validate a judge

reading_paths.description: Use to set an acceptance gate for agent-produced work: define claims and evidence, exercise product behavior, inspect checks and their oracles, and set feedback and integration gates. For additional guarantees or review decisions, branch to formal-verification-and-executable-constraints or code-review-and-organizational-risk respectively.
reading_paths.title: Decide what evidence supports accepting agent work

reading_paths.description: Use when selecting evidence with domain experts: start with domain success and accountability, then choose the article for your workflow rather than reading all branches. The remaining articles are alternatives for financial work, grounded answers, voice, clinical review, legal documents, synthetic respondents, visual or physical systems, creative work, or recommendations.
reading_paths.title: Evaluate a domain-specific workflow

reading_paths.description: Use before granting or expanding agent autonomy: prioritize harms and exposure, model threats, select independently enforced controls, establish human oversight, probe behavior, then decide release. Optional privacy-tenancy-and-data-governance covers sensitive data; specific attack and payment workflows remain in the safety section index.
reading_paths.title: Set risk-based agent controls and release authority

reading_paths.description: Use when a deployed agent is failing or changing: define useful outcomes, monitor live quality, diagnose the failure, turn evidence into regression tests, decide release, and continue monitoring. Optional build-and-maintain-production-grounded-evaluation-sets explains how to maintain cases; runtime architecture and operations can be browsed in the production section.
reading_paths.title: Turn production failures into a release decision

reading_paths.description: Use for a task-level model-selection or routing decision: compare useful work, cost and quality; select model/runtime candidates and routing; run controlled regression evidence; decide promotion. Optional inference-serving addresses serving capacity or latency, and training-and-distillation addresses weight changes; neither is required for routine routing.
reading_paths.title: Choose and release a cost-effective model route

reading_paths.description: Use after observing a failure: diagnose it, design controlled improvement evidence, protect the objective and holdout, choose an intervention, verify regressions, then decide promotion. Prompt/harness, retrieval and training articles are alternatives chosen for the diagnosed bottleneck, not consecutive required steps.
reading_paths.title: Improve a failing system without gaming the score
